analysis.title: Misconception Buster: Breathing ≠ Respiration
analysis.description: A two-column comparison slide contrasting Ventilation (Breathing) with Cellular Respiration across process type, location, and purpose, with supporting icon illustrations for lungs and mitochondrion.
analysis.layout: The title is centred at the top. The body is split into two equal columns divided by a dashed vertical line: the left column covers 'Ventilation (Breathing)' with a blue lung graphic and a three-row comparative table/list, and the right column covers 'Cellular Respiration' with a glowing green mitochondrion graphic and corresponding rows.

components.visibleText:
Ventilation (Breathing)
Type of process: Physical mechanical mechanism.
Location: Only in the lungs (specialised organs).
Purpose: Gas exchange (moving oxygen into the blood and carbon dioxide out).

Cellular Respiration
Type of process: Universal chemical process.
Location: Inside all living cells (specifically the mitochondria).
Purpose: Releasing trapped chemical energy (ATP) to power the cell.
